title: Plans & the future
goal: Talk about your plans, say what you want, intend and will probably do, and make arrangements.
intro:
Nepali has several ways of talking about the future, and everyday speech prefers the softer ones. The plain present (**म भोलि जान्छु** 'I'll go tomorrow') covers firm plans; the **-ला** forms (**म जाउँला** 'I'll probably go') are for likely or hoped-for events; and the **-नेछ** future (**म जानेछु**) sounds definite and formal, like the news.

You'll also learn how to express wanting and intending: **-न चाहन्छु**, **-न मन छ**, **-ने विचार छ**. Our dialogue looks ahead to **Dashain**, Nepal's biggest festival.

vocab.note: सपना देख्नु 'to dream' (lit. see a dream).
म जान चाहन्छु 'I want to go' (a bit formal). Compare चाहिनु 'to be needed'.
मलाई नाच्न मन लाग्यो 'I feel like dancing'.
Also -ने विचार छ 'I intend to' (विचार, unit 14).
आउने हप्ता 'next week', आउने साल 'next year'.
सुरु गर्नु 'to start (something)', सुरु हुनु 'to begin'.
दसैं बिदा 'Dashain holidays'; बिदा दिनु 'to see someone off'.
From हुनु. ऊ घरमा होला 'he's probably at home'.
नयाँ घरमा सर्नु 'to move into a new house'.

phrases.en: What are your plans for tomorrow?
I'd like to travel around Nepal.
I want to learn Nepali well.
We'll see — if I can, I'll come.
Have you booked the ticket yet?

grammar.title: Three ways to talk about the future
grammar.body:
**1. The present habitual** for firm plans and the near future: म भोलि **जान्छु** 'I'm going tomorrow'. The present continuous works too: म भोलि **जाँदै छु**.

**2. The probable future -ला** — the everyday 'will', with a shade of 'probably / I expect':
म **गरुँला** *garuṃlā* · हामी **गरौँला** *garauṃlā*
तिमी **गर्लाऊ** *garlāu* · ऊ **गर्ला** *garlā* · उनी/उनीहरू **गर्लान्** *garlān*
तपाईं/उहाँ **गर्नुहोला** *garnuholā*
Vowel stems: जानु → **जाउँला, जाला, जालान्, जानुहोला**; आउनु → **आउँला, आउला**. It's also used for guesses about the present: ऊ घरमा **होला** 'he's probably at home'. With तपाईं it makes a gentle request: आउनुहोला 'please do come'.

**3. The definite future -नेछ** — formal, written, news-style:
म **गर्नेछु** · हामी **गर्नेछौँ** · तिमी **गर्नेछौ** · ऊ **गर्नेछ** · उनीहरू **गर्नेछन्** · तपाईं **गर्नुहुनेछ**.
Negative: गर्नेछैन, or more commonly the present negative गर्दिनँ / गर्दैन.

examples.en: I'm going to India next month.
He's probably at the office now.
The Prime Minister will go to India tomorrow. (news style)

grammar.title: Wanting, intending and 'going to'
grammar.body:
• **-न चाहनु** 'want to' (neutral, a bit formal): म विदेश **जान चाहन्छु**.
• **-न मन छ / मन लाग्छ** 'would like to, feel like' (experiencer, very common in speech): **मलाई** पौडी खेल्न **मन छ**; आज केही गर्न मन लागेन 'I didn't feel like doing anything today'.
• **-ने विचार/योजना छ** 'plan/intend to': मेरो नेपाल बस्ने **विचार छ** 'I'm thinking of living in Nepal'.
• **-ने** alone in questions = 'shall we / are you going to': के **खाने**? 'what shall we eat?', कहिले **जाने**? 'when are we going?'.
• **-न लागेको** 'about to': म निस्कन लागेको, एकछिन पर्खनुहोस् 'I'm about to leave, wait a moment'.
• **-इसक्नु** 'already (completed)': मैले टिकट किनिसकेँ 'I've already bought the ticket'.

examples.en: I want to become a doctor.

examples.native: मलाई आज बाहिर खान मन छ।
examples.roman: malāi āja bāhira khāna man chha.
examples.en: I'd like to eat out today.

examples.native: हाम्रो अर्को साल घर बनाउने योजना छ।
examples.roman: hāmro arko sāl ghar banāune yojanā chha.
examples.en: We plan to build a house next year.
What shall we cook this evening?
The bus is about to leave — quick!

dialogue.title: Dashain plans
dialogue.setting: A few weeks before Dashain, Bikash and Tom talk about their holiday plans.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.en: What are your plans for Dashain?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: मेरो अन्नपूर्ण बेस क्याम्प जाने विचार छ।
lines.roman: mero Annapurna Bes Kyāmp jāne bichār chha.
lines.en: I'm thinking of going to Annapurna Base Camp.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.en: Great! When are you setting off?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: असोज बीस गते पोखराबाट सुरु गर्छु। तपाईं नि?
lines.roman: asoj bis gate Pokharābāṭa suru garchhu. tapāiṃ ni?
lines.en: I'll start from Pokhara on the 20th of Asoj. And you?

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: म गाउँ जान्छु। दसैंमा सबै परिवार भेला हुन्छ।
lines.roman: ma gāuṃ jānchhu. Dasaiṃmā sabai pariwār bhelā hunchha.
lines.en: I'm going to my village. At Dashain the whole family gets together.

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: गोरखामा। टीका लगाएर म दस गतेतिर फर्कुँला।
lines.roman: Gorkhāmā. ṭikā lagāera ma das gatetira pharkuṃlā.
lines.en: In Gorkha. After receiving tika I'll probably come back around the tenth.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: ट्रेकपछि म पनि तपाईंको गाउँ आउन सक्छु?
lines.roman: ṭrekpachhi ma pani tapāiṃko gāuṃ āuna sakchhu?
lines.en: After the trek, could I come to your village too?

lines.speaker: Bikash
lines.native: पक्कै पनि! आमा धेरै खुसी हुनुहुनेछ।
lines.roman: pakkai pani! āmā dherai khusi hunuhunechha.
lines.en: Of course! My mother will be delighted.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.native: कस्तो रमाइलो होला! म अवश्य आउँछु।
lines.roman: kasto ramāilo holā! ma abasya āuṃchhu.
lines.en: That'll be such fun! I'll definitely come.

culture: **Dashain** (दसैं, in Asoj/Kattik) is Nepal's biggest festival: offices close, cities empty as people travel home, and on the tenth day (**दशमी**) elders put red **टीका** (rice, yoghurt and vermilion) on younger relatives' foreheads and give them **जमरा** (barley shoots) and blessings. Families feast on goat meat, children fly kites and play on giant bamboo swings (**पिङ**). A few weeks later comes **Tihar** (तिहार), the festival of lights, when crows, dogs and cows are honoured, homes are lit for the goddess Laxmi, and sisters give their brothers **भाइटीका**. Important dates — weddings, journeys, moving house — are often fixed by an astrologer for an auspicious time (**साइत**).
